title: Call Web API from JavaScript with XMLHttpRequest (XHR)
description: Consume ASP.NET Core Web APIs from client-side JavaScript using the XMLHttpRequest (XHR) object for all CRUD operations.

data.text: Why Call a Web API from JavaScript?

A Web API is most useful when a **client application** can communicate with it. **JavaScript** running in the browser is the most common client. Using JavaScript you can fetch data, display it in the DOM, collect user input, and send it back — all without reloading the page.

data.title: XMLHttpRequest (XHR)
data.text: XMLHttpRequest is the browser API for making HTTP calls from JavaScript. Despite its name it works with any data format — JSON, XML, or plain text — not just XML. It is the foundation of what we now call AJAX (Asynchronous JavaScript and XML).
Client-Server Flow

data.caption: JavaScript XHR calls to an ASP.NET Core Web API for each CRUD operation.
data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
    participant JS as JavaScript (XHR)
    participant API as ASP.NET Core Web API
    JS->>API: GET /api/Reservation
    API-->>JS: JSON array of reservations
    JS->>API: POST /api/Reservation (new reservation JSON)
    API-->>JS: Created reservation with Id
    JS->>API: PUT /api/Reservation (updated reservation)
    API-->>JS: Updated reservation JSON
    JS->>API: PATCH /api/Reservation/1 (patch document)
    API-->>JS: 200 OK
    JS->>API: DELETE /api/Reservation/1
    API-->>JS: 204 No Content

data.text: The XMLHttpRequest Object — Step by Step
Every XHR call follows the same four-step pattern regardless of the HTTP verb:

data.title: Four steps to call any API with XHR
items: **Create** the XHR object: `const xhttp = new XMLHttpRequest();`
**Send** the request: `xhttp.send(body);` — body is optional for GET and DELETE.
**Handle the response** via the `onreadystatechange` event listener, checking for `readyState === 4` and `status === 200`.

data.text: GET — Fetch All Reservations
The GET verb retrieves data. No request body is needed. The API returns a JSON array of all reservations. We display them inside an HTML `<table>`.

data.title: readyState values
data.text: readyState 4 means the request is complete. Always combine it with status 200 before processing the response — other statuses (404, 500) mean something went wrong.
GET by Id — Search a Single Reservation
To fetch one reservation, append its `id` to the URL path. The API returns a single JSON object or a 400 status if the id is missing or zero.

data.text: POST — Create a New Reservation

A **POST** request sends new data in the **request body** as JSON. Before sending, convert the JavaScript object to a JSON string using `JSON.stringify()`. Set the `Content-Type` header to `application/json`.

data.text: PUT — Fully Replace a Reservation
**PUT** replaces the entire reservation record. All fields must be included in the request body, typically as `FormData` when the server expects `[FromForm]`.

data.content: Form pre-populated with existing reservation values.
data.code: ID Name Start Location End Location

data.content: Load the existing reservation by id, then send all fields back as FormData on PUT.

data.text: PATCH — Partially Update a Reservation

**PATCH** is for updating only specific fields without sending the entire object. The request body is a **JSON Patch document** — an array of operations. Each operation has an `op` (e.g. `"replace"`), a `path` (the field name), and a `value` (the new value).

data.title: JavaScript — PATCH specific fields
data.content: Build a JSON Patch document and send it with Content-Type application/json-patch+json.
data.code:
<script>
    function GetReservation() {
        const params = new URL(document.location).searchParams;
        const id = params.get("id");
        const xhttp = new XMLHttpRequest();
        xhttp.open("GET", `https://localhost:44324/api/Reservation/${id}`, true);
        xhttp.send();
        xhttp.onreadystatechange = function () {
            if (this.readyState === 4 && this.status === 200) {
                const r = JSON.parse(this.responseText);
                document.getElementById("Name").value = r.name;
                document.getElementById("StartLocation").value = r.startLocation;
            }
        };
    }
    GetReservation();

    document.getElementById("UpdateButton").addEventListener("click", function () {
        const params = new URL(document.location).searchParams;
        const id = params.get("id");

        const patchData = JSON.stringify([
            { op: "replace", path: "Name", value: document.getElementById("Name").value },
            { op: "replace", path: "StartLocation", value: document.getElementById("StartLocation").value },
            { op: "replace", path: "EndLocation", value: document.getElementById("EndLocation").value }
        ]);

        const xhttp = new XMLHttpRequest();
        xhttp.open("PATCH", `https://localhost:44324/api/Reservation/${id}`, true);
        xhttp.setRequestHeader("Content-Type", "application/json-patch+json");
        xhttp.send(patchData);
        xhttp.onreadystatechange = function () {
            if (this.readyState === 4 && this.status === 200) {
                window.location.href = "AllReservation.html";
            }
        };
    });
</script>

data.text: DELETE — Remove a Reservation

A **DELETE** request needs only the reservation id in the URL. No request body is required. After a successful delete the API returns **204 No Content**. We add a delete icon to each table row and attach a click event dynamically.

data.title: JavaScript — DELETE with dynamic click events
data.content: Attach a click event to each delete icon, read the id from the row, and call the DELETE endpoint.

data.text: Upload an Image File to the API
Web APIs can also accept **file uploads** using the `IFormFile` type on the server. From JavaScript, you attach the file to a `FormData` object and send it with XHR.

data.title: C# — API endpoint for file upload
data.content: Server-side action that receives a file and saves it to wwwroot/Images.

data.title: AddFile.html — File upload form
data.content: HTML with a file input and upload button.

data.title: JavaScript — Upload file with FormData
data.content: Read the selected file, wrap it in FormData, and POST it to the API.
data.code:
<script>
    document.getElementById("AddButton").addEventListener("click", function () {
        const fileInput = document.getElementById("File");
        const formData = new FormData();
        formData.append("file", fileInput.files[0]);

        const xhttp = new XMLHttpRequest();
        xhttp.open("POST", "https://localhost:44324/api/Reservation/UploadFile", true);
        xhttp.send(formData);

        xhttp.onreadystatechange = function () {
            if (this.readyState === 4 && this.status === 200) {
                const imageUrl = this.responseText;
                const img = document.getElementById("uploadedImage");
                img.src = imageUrl;
                img.style.display = "block";
            }
        };
    });
</script>

items.text: GET by id appends the id to the API URL.
POST uses JSON.stringify() and sets Content-Type to application/json.
PUT uses FormData to send all fields.
PATCH sends a JSON Patch array with Content-Type application/json-patch+json.

items.question: When should I use FormData vs JSON.stringify()?
items.answer: Use JSON.stringify() when the API expects JSON in the body (most POST endpoints with [FromBody]). Use FormData when the API expects multipart/form-data — typically when uploading files or when [FromForm] is used on the server parameter.

items.question: What Content-Type do I use for PATCH?
items.answer: Use application/json-patch+json. This tells the server the body contains a JSON Patch document per RFC 6902.

items.question: How do I handle errors from the API?
items.answer: Check this.status inside onreadystatechange. Status codes 400, 401, 404, and 500 indicate errors. Use this.responseText to read any error message the API returned.

items.question: Can I use XHR in a modern codebase?
items.answer: XHR works everywhere but the modern alternative is the Fetch API with async/await. The concepts are the same — XHR is still valid to learn and works in older browsers.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: XMLHttpRequest follows a four-step pattern: create, open, send, and handle the response.
Always check readyState === 4 and status === 200 before processing the response.
Use JSON.stringify() and Content-Type: application/json for JSON request bodies.
Use FormData for file uploads and [FromForm] server parameters.
PATCH uses a JSON Patch document with op, path, and value entries.
data.takeaway: You can now build rich JavaScript pages that perform full CRUD operations against an ASP.NET Core Web API using XHR.
